name: Spawn Global Entity
desc: Spawns a global entity visible to all players (lightning bolt).

writeup.p: Spawns a globally visible entity, in 1.8.9 exclusively the lightning bolt. The server broadcasts it to every player within 512 blocks of the strike (WorldServer.addWeatherEffect via sendToAllNear). The client handler converts the x32 fixed-point coordinates and, when the type byte is 1, instantiates an EntityLightningBolt in the client world. Because the entity is server-created and broadcast, it is the only lightning representation the client ever sees.

NetHandlerPlayClient.handleSpawnGlobalEntity divides each coordinate by 32.0D and builds an EntityLightningBolt only when the type byte equals 1; any other type yields a null entity and is dropped. The bolt is then added to the client world, which drives its ambient light flash and thunder sound. Server-side the packet constructor derives entityId, coordinates and type from the Entity argument passed in by WorldServer.

Exactly one module-grade consumer in the corpus: Rise 6.1.30 and 6.2.4 LightningTracker, an exploit-category module that prints the strike coordinates and distance to chat on every type-1 packet. It is informational, not an ESP. Every other client in the corpus (Memeware, Nekoware, Sigma, Spicy, Tenacity) references the packet only through vanilla NetHandlerPlayClient, confirming the context note: lightning handling is vanilla across the board.

The packet is a broadcast with a server-chosen entityId and position, so a malicious server can spam it to fake lightning at arbitrary coordinates; there is no client-side validation beyond the type check. The 512-block broadcast radius means a strike far outside the client's render distance still spawns an entity. No client in the corpus abuses this for teleport hacks or lightning-based exploits, and none uses it for anti-cheat purposes.

implementation.overview: The lightning broadcast packet, vanilla everywhere in the corpus except Rise 6.x's LightningTracker, which prints strike coordinates and distance to chat. No ESP, no weather control, no exploit use: the 8 clients confirm this packet is near-invisible to module authors.
implementation.server_handling: WorldServer.addWeatherEffect calls ConfigurationManager.sendToAllNear with a 512.0D radius on the strike position, same dimension, constructing S2CPacketSpawnGlobalEntity from the EntityLightningBolt. The packet's constructor copies entityId, x*32, y*32, z*32 and type (1 for lightning) from the entity. NetHandlerPlayClient only materializes the bolt when type == 1, ignoring the entityId for lookup since the client creates the entity fresh.
implementation.protocol_notes: Encoding: VarInt entityId, int x*32, int y*32, int z*32, byte type. Coordinates are fixed-point at 1/32 block resolution, finer than S29's 1/8. The type byte is the only discriminator; in 1.8.9 only 1 (lightning) is ever sent. The packet predates the generic Packet<T> signature in the older clients (raw Packet with double dispatch) while Rise 6.x uses Packet<INetHandlerPlayClient>.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: No anti-cheat touches this packet. Lightning is ambient weather; there is no cheat surface to measure. The only observable abuse would be server-side strike spam to distract or desync clients, which no module in the corpus defends against. The 512-block radius is worth noting for anyone building lightning-based radar: strikes beyond render distance still arrive.

modules.name: LightningTracker
modules.purpose: Print a chat message with the coordinates and distance of every lightning strike.
modules.how_it_works: A PacketReceiveEvent listener. For each S2C it divides the x32 coordinates back to blocks, rounds to two decimals, and when the type byte is 1 calls ChatUtil.display with the position and the player's distance to the strike. It is an exploit-category module but performs no world manipulation.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Passive and read-only; nothing is sent or cancelled. No server can detect it.
modules.variations: Identical file in Rise 6.1.30. Rise 5.99 has no equivalent module, and no other client in the corpus references this packet outside vanilla code.

implementation.general_hooks: Single consumer: Rise 6.x PacketReceiveEvent listener inside the module.
implementation.client_variations: Rise 6.1.30 and 6.2.4 ship byte-identical LightningTracker files. The other six clients touch the packet only in net/minecraft vanilla sources (NetHandlerPlayClient, EnumConnectionState, WorldServer).

anticheat.overview: No anticheat in the 50-repo corpus runs a check on the global-entity (lightning) packet. The only genuine packet references are framework registrations: Artemis wraps PacketPlayOutSpawnEntityWeather as GPacketPlayServerSpawnEntityWeather and registers it at SERVER_PLAY + 69, and Negativity lists the packet in its PacketType enum. Every other corpus hit is keyword noise from the search term Lightning: strikeLightningEffect ban-punishment visuals in PeyangSuperbAntiCheat KickUtil, TruthfulAC Check and SafeguardAC ViolationHandler, and lightning-rod block-shape comments in NoCheatPlus. Lightning is ambient server weather with no client-trust signal, so nothing measures it.
